questions.question_text: Explain the following terms: i) Coeff. of Compressibility ii) Compression Index iii) Coefficient of volume Compressibility iv) Degree of Consolidation v) Coeff. of Consolidation.
Draw contact pressure diagram for surface and deep footing in clay for flexible and rigid footing.

An oedometer test gives time for 90% consolidation as 16 minutes on a 20 mm thick specimen (double drainage). Determine the time required for 50% consolidation for a clay bed 3m thick with single face drainage.
Discuss with sketch, logarithm of time fitting method for determination of coefficient of consolidation.
Explain the following terms: i) Normally consolidated soil ii) Pre consolidated soil iii) Under consolidated soil.

The overburden pressure at the middle of 7.5 mm thick clayey layer increased from 2kg/cm2 to 3.5kg/cm2. Find the settlement due to consolidation assuming liquid limit and initial void ratio of the clay as 36% and 0.82 respectively.
Discuss the necessity of pile foundation.
What is negative skin friction? How it is calculated for single pile embedded in two layers of clay.
20 piles are arranged in four rows and five columns. Calculate the efficiency of the pile group by Feld’s rule.
Explain the procedure for calculation of bearing capacity of single pile by static method?
Discuss static pile load test.
A circular pile with 0.35m diameter and 10m length penetrates a deposit of clay having cohesion 5 kN/m2 and mobilizing factor of 0.8. Calculate the ultimate frictional resistance of the pile.
Explain design steps of raft foundation by conventional (rigid) method.
Draw well foundation and state the function of each component.
Write a note on i) Uses of caissons ii) Sand island method
Explain the steps involved in proportioning of isolated footing.

Discuss the design principle of undreamed pile.

Describe engineering problems associated with black cotton soil.

The inner diameters of sampling tube and that of cutting edge are 72 mm and 70 mm respectively. Their outer diameters are 74 mm and 76 mm respectively. Determine the inside clearance, outside clearance and area ratio of sampler. Comment on suitability of sampler.
Discuss IS Criteria for depth of bore holes in subsurface investigations.

Discuss the modes of shear failure.
Plate load test was conducted on a square plate of size 0.3 mm in clay. The settlement observed was 4 mm. Determine the settlement of square footing of size 2 m under the same load intensity.

Explain the effect of water table on bearing capacity.
Explain spring analogy with respect with respect to consolidation process.
Explain with sketches how contact pressure changes according to type of soil and type of footing.

A soil stratum is 10 m thick with pervious stratum on top and bottom. Determine the time required for 50% consolidation. Use following data (i) coefficient of permeability of soil = 10-9 m/s.(ii) Coefficient of compression = 0.003 m2/kN. (iii) void ratio =2.

A rectangular footing 2 m × 3 m carries a column load of 600 kN at a depth of 1 m. The footing rests on c -  soil strata, 6 m thick having Poisson’s ratio of 0.25 and Young’s modulus of elasticity as 20000 kN/m2 . Calculate the immediate elastic settlement of the footing. Take influence factor = 1.06.

What is the principle used in dynamic methods to calculate pile capacity? Write Engineering News Formula with meaning of each term.
Explain the static pile load test in detail.

A 3 × 3 pile group with pile diameter and pile length of 300 mm and 10 m respectively is embedded in soft clay with cohesion of 70 kN/m2. The spacing between the piles (both ways) is 90 cm and adhesion factor is 0.6. Calculate the capacity of the pile group. Take factor of safety = 2.5. Neglect end bearing.

A normally consolidated clay stratum of 5m thickness has two permeable layers at its top and bottom. The liquid limit and the initial void ratio of clay are 40% and 0.85 respectively. While the initial overburden pressure at the middle of clay layers is 300kPa. Due to the construction of a new building, this pressure increases by 150 kPa. Compute the probable primary consolidation settlement (expressed in mm) of the building.

An undisturbed sample of clay 24mm thick consolidated 50% in 20 minutes when tested in the laboratory, with drainage allowed at the top and bottom. The clay layer from which the sample was obtained is 4m tick in the field. How much time will it take place to consolidate 50% with a single drain?
